title: Interactive rollout sandbox empty state — in-product simulation for cost-aware onboarding
creator: Aisha Verma
description:
Problem: New users land on the Rollouts page with an empty state and no safe, low-friction way to learn how Canary/Canary+Fallback works alongside cost implications. Current empty states are static and only surface docs links.

Goal: Design an interactive, contextual 'Rollout Sandbox' empty state that lets users: (1) run a short guided simulation of a canary rollout using a sample traffic profile, (2) preview token-level cost estimates and projected latency during the simulated rollout, and (3) see inline tips/tooltips that explain tradeoffs and guardrails (percent traffic, fallback policy, cost threshold). This should be discoverable during onboarding, accessible from empty states, and usable without provisioning Dedicated capacity.

Scope: UI/UX flows for the empty state card and the modal sandbox; prototypes for three scenarios (quick demo, cost-focused walkthrough, advanced config); tooltip text/content; microcopy for CTAs and warnings; acceptance criteria and usability testing script. Engineering feasibility check for simulated traffic and cost estimation algorithm is required but out of scope to implement in this ticket beyond API contract proposals.
acceptance_criteria: Empty state shows a prominent 'Try Rollout Sandbox' CTA and a short 1-line description
Clicking CTA opens a sandbox modal with three preset scenarios: Quick Demo, Cost Preview, and Advanced Config
Sandbox runs a time-limited simulated rollout (visualization only) without affecting live models or billing — simulation UI shows estimated tokens and projected cost range
Inline tooltips explain percent traffic, KV cache cold start impact, batching implications, and automatic fallback behavior
Prototype (Figma + clickable prototype) tested with 6 PM/engineer participants and 8 new users; usability issues logged and addressed
Design handoff includes component specs, accessibility notes (keyboard focus, aria labels), and copy package for engineering
decisions: Use modal-first sandbox (lightweight) rather than a full-new page to reduce discovery friction
Provide only simulation of metrics (no real traffic or billing) for first pass to avoid security and billing complexity
Surface cost as a projected band (low/median/high) with a simple explainer rather than precise dollar amounts to avoid false precision
Include two failsafe CTAs: 'Run Demo' and 'Open Advanced Config' — advanced config requires a secondary confirmation explaining production differences
Tooltips to include links to deeper docs for Dedicated and Private deployment constraints instead of embedding all details

usability_findings: Participants found the initial cost numbers confusing; median/low/high bands improved comprehension
Users expected the sandbox to indicate whether changes would persist — added clear 'simulation only' banner solved this
Some participants attempted to change model weights in the demo — added disabled advanced controls with tooltip explaining why live changes require Dedicated capacity
